96	async def create_draft_entry(
97	    session: AsyncSession,
98	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
99	    payload: JournalEntryCreate,
100	    *,
101	    functional_amounts: list[tuple[Decimal, Decimal]] | None = None,
102	) -> JournalEntry:
103	    """Create a DRAFT entry + lines (D-017). Validates: >= 2 lines, each one-sided, all accounts
104	    exist + postable + same tenant. Registers the document (no number; claimed at posting, D-012).
105	    Does NOT claim a number / resolve the period — both at posting.
106	
107	    Default: functional == transaction, balanced in TRANSACTION terms (the posting protocol then
108	    translates FX). With explicit ``functional_amounts`` ((debit, credit) per line; AP/AR clearing,
109	    D-019) those become the functional amounts and the balance check is on the FUNCTIONAL sums — a
110	    mixed-currency clearing entry balances only in functional, posted with skip_translation."""
111	    if len(payload.lines) < 2:
112	        raise ValidationFailedError(
113	            message="A journal entry needs at least two lines",
114	            code="finance.journal_too_few_lines",
115	        )
116	
117	    for index, line in enumerate(payload.lines, start=1):
118	        _assert_line_one_sided(line, index)
119	    # Balance on transaction sides by default, on explicit functional sides for a (mixed-currency)
120	    # clearing entry where only functional must balance.
121	    sides = functional_amounts or [
122	        (ln.transaction_debit_amount, ln.transaction_credit_amount) for ln in payload.lines
123	    ]
124	    total_debit = sum((d for d, _c in sides), Decimal(0))
125	    total_credit = sum((c for _d, c in sides), Decimal(0))
126	    if total_debit != total_credit:
127	        raise ValidationFailedError(
128	            message="Journal entry debits and credits must balance",
129	            code="finance.journal_unbalanced",
130	            details={"total_debit": str(total_debit), "total_credit": str(total_credit)},
131	        )
132	
133	    account_ids = {line.account_id for line in payload.lines}
134	    await _require_postable_accounts(session, tenant_id, account_ids)
135	    entry_id = uuid.uuid4()
136	    document = await docflow.register_document(
137	        session,
138	        tenant_id,
139	        JOURNAL_ENTRY_DOC_TYPE,
140	        entry_id,
141	        doc_number=None,
142	        status=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value,
143	    )
144	    entry = JournalEntry(
145	        id=entry_id,
146	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
147	        document_id=document.id,
148	        posting_date=payload.posting_date,
149	        currency_code=payload.currency_code,
150	        description=payload.description,
151	        document_type=DocumentType(payload.document_type).value,
152	        status=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value,
153	    )
154	    session.add(entry)
155	    for index, line in enumerate(payload.lines, start=1):
156	        # ``sides`` is functional == transaction by default (posting translates FX), or the explicit
157	        # clearing functional amounts when supplied — either way one (debit, credit) per line.
158	        func_debit, func_credit = sides[index - 1]
159	        session.add(
160	            JournalLine(
161	                tenant_id=tenant_id,
162	                journal_entry_id=entry_id,
163	                line_number=index,
164	                account_id=line.account_id,
165	                description=line.description,
166	                transaction_debit_amount=line.transaction_debit_amount,
167	                transaction_credit_amount=line.transaction_credit_amount,
168	                functional_debit_amount=func_debit,
169	                functional_credit_amount=func_credit,
170	                currency_code=payload.currency_code,
171	                cost_center_id=line.cost_center_id,
172	                profit_center_id=line.profit_center_id,
173	                project_id=line.project_id,
174	                item_id=line.item_id,
175	                partner_type=line.partner_type,
176	                partner_id=line.partner_id,
177	            )
178	        )
179	    await session.flush()
180	    return entry
181	
182	
183	async def post_entry(
184	    session: AsyncSession,
185	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
186	    entry_id: uuid.UUID,
187	    *,
188	    rate_override: Decimal | None = None,
189	    skip_translation: bool = False,
190	) -> JournalEntry:
191	    """THE posting protocol (D-017 two-flush). Validates DRAFT + balanced, resolves + checks the
192	    open period from posting_date (422 before touching the DB), translates foreign-currency
193	    functional amounts (D-019; an explicit ``rate_override`` wins over the looked-up SPOT rate),
194	    claims the gapless number in this transaction, then flushes the loaded lines (still DRAFT) and
195	    finally the POSTED header (balance + period triggers fire there). Publishes JournalEntryPosted;
196	
197	    ``skip_translation`` (D-019, used by AP/AR clearing): the caller has ALREADY set each line's
198	    functional amounts (e.g. a payment clears its open items at the bill's frozen rate while the
199	    bank is at the payment rate, with a realized-FX line absorbing the difference). The engine then
200	    only validates those pre-computed functional amounts balance, never re-rating them — the one
201	    case where functional != transaction × a single entry rate.
202	    the caller commits via uow."""
203	    entry = await get_entry(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
204	    if entry.status != EntryStatus.DRAFT.value:
205	        raise ConflictError(
206	            message="Only a draft journal entry can be posted",
207	            code="finance.journal_not_draft",
208	            details={"status": entry.status},
209	        )
210	
211	    lines = await load_lines(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
212	    if len(lines) < 2:
213	        raise ValidationFailedError(
214	            message="A journal entry needs at least two lines",
215	            code="finance.journal_too_few_lines",
216	        )
217	
218	    # FX translation (D-019): recompute functional amounts at the posting rate when the entry is in
219	    # a foreign currency, balancing the functional residual into the largest line. After this the
220	    # functional sums (which the balance trigger checks) are exact and equal. Skipped when the
221	    # caller pre-computed functional amounts (AP/AR clearing realized FX) — the balance check below
222	    # then validates those.
223	    if not skip_translation:
224	        await translate_entry_lines(session, tenant_id, entry, lines, rate_override)
225	
226	    debit, credit = entry_totals(lines)
227	    if debit != credit or debit <= 0:
228	        raise ValidationFailedError(
229	            message="Journal entry debits and credits must balance and be positive",
230	            code="finance.journal_unbalanced",
231	            details={"total_debit": str(debit), "total_credit": str(credit)},
232	        )
233	
234	    # Period resolution + open check FIRST (service-level half of D-018); the trigger backstops.
235	    period = await queries.find_period_for_date(session, tenant_id, entry.posting_date)
236	    if period is None or period.status != PeriodStatus.OPEN.value:
237	        raise ValidationFailedError(
238	            message="The posting date is not within an open fiscal period",
239	            code="finance.period_closed",
240	            details={"posting_date": entry.posting_date.isoformat()},
241	        )
242	
243	    # Claim the gapless number in this transaction (D-012): gapless because the claim and the
244	    # POSTED commit succeed or roll back together.
245	    await ensure_sequence(
246	        session,
247	        tenant_id,
248	        JOURNAL_SEQUENCE_NAME,
249	        JOURNAL_NUMBER_PREFIX,
250	        JOURNAL_NUMBER_PADDING,
251	        year_reset=True,
252	    )
253	    entry_number = await claim_number(
254	        session, tenant_id, JOURNAL_SEQUENCE_NAME, on_date=entry.posting_date
255	    )
256	
257	    # Flush 1: denormalize onto the loaded lines while the entry is still DRAFT.
258	    for line in lines:
259	        line.is_posted = True
260	        line.posting_date = entry.posting_date
261	        line.fiscal_period_id = period.id
262	    await session.flush()
263	
264	    # Flush 2: promote the header. The period + balance triggers fire on this DRAFT->POSTED UPDATE.
265	    entry.entry_number = entry_number
266	    entry.fiscal_period_id = period.id
267	    entry.status = EntryStatus.POSTED.value
268	    entry.posted_at = datetime.now(UTC)
269	    await session.flush()
270	
271	    await docflow.set_document_status(
272	        session,
273	        tenant_id,
274	        entry.document_id,
275	        status=EntryStatus.POSTED.value,
276	        doc_number=entry_number,
277	    )
278	
279	    publish(
280	        session,
281	        JournalEntryPosted(
282	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
283	            entry_id=entry.id,
284	            entry_number=entry_number,
285	            document_type=entry.document_type,
286	            posting_date=entry.posting_date.isoformat(),
287	            currency_code=entry.currency_code,
288	            total_functional_amount=debit,
289	            account_ids=tuple(line.account_id for line in lines),
290	        ),
291	    )
292	    return entry
293	
294	
295	async def reverse_entry(
296	    session: AsyncSession,
297	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
298	    entry_id: uuid.UUID,
299	    reversal_date: date,
300	    description: str | None = None,
301	) -> JournalEntry:
302	    """Reverse a POSTED entry (D-017). Creates a NEW same-document_type entry with each line's
303	    debit/credit SWAPPED, posts it into ``reversal_date``'s open period (its own number), then
304	    sets the original REVERSED + reversed_by_entry_id — the ONLY mutation the immutability trigger
305	    permits. Links the two documents ('reverses'), publishes JournalEntryReversed, returns the
306	    reversing entry."""
307	    original = await get_entry(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
308	    if original.status != EntryStatus.POSTED.value:
309	        raise ConflictError(
310	            message="Only a posted journal entry can be reversed",
311	            code="finance.journal_not_posted",
312	            details={"status": original.status},
313	        )
314	    if original.reversed_by_entry_id is not None:
315	        raise ConflictError(
316	            message="This journal entry has already been reversed",
317	            code="finance.journal_already_reversed",
318	        )
319	
320	    original_lines = await load_lines(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
321	
322	    reversal_id = uuid.uuid4()
323	    reversal_document = await docflow.register_document(
324	        session,
325	        tenant_id,
326	        JOURNAL_ENTRY_DOC_TYPE,
327	        reversal_id,
328	        doc_number=None,
329	        status=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value,
330	    )
331	    reversal = JournalEntry(
332	        id=reversal_id,
333	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
334	        document_id=reversal_document.id,
335	        posting_date=reversal_date,
336	        currency_code=original.currency_code,
337	        description=description
338	        or f"Reversal of {original.entry_number or original.id}",
339	        document_type=original.document_type,
340	        status=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value,
341	        reverses_entry_id=original.id,
342	    )
343	    session.add(reversal)
344	    for line in original_lines:
345	        session.add(
346	            JournalLine(
347	                tenant_id=tenant_id,
348	                journal_entry_id=reversal_id,
349	                line_number=line.line_number,
350	                account_id=line.account_id,
351	                description=line.description,
352	                # Swap debit <-> credit in both currency pairs (frozen functional amounts).
353	                transaction_debit_amount=line.transaction_credit_amount,
354	                transaction_credit_amount=line.transaction_debit_amount,
355	                functional_debit_amount=line.functional_credit_amount,
356	                functional_credit_amount=line.functional_debit_amount,
357	                currency_code=line.currency_code,
358	                cost_center_id=line.cost_center_id,
359	                profit_center_id=line.profit_center_id,
360	                project_id=line.project_id,
361	                item_id=line.item_id,
362	                partner_type=line.partner_type,
363	                partner_id=line.partner_id,
364	            )
365	        )
366	    await session.flush()
367	
368	    # Post the reversing entry (claims its own number, runs the same period/balance checks).
369	    await post_entry(session, tenant_id, reversal_id)
370	
371	    # The single sanctioned mutation on a POSTED original (immutability trigger permits exactly
372	    # this: status POSTED->REVERSED with reversed_by_entry_id set).
373	    original.reversed_by_entry_id = reversal_id
374	    original.status = EntryStatus.REVERSED.value
375	    await session.flush()
376	
377	    await docflow.set_document_status(
378	        session, tenant_id, original.document_id, status=EntryStatus.REVERSED.value
379	    )
380	    await docflow.link_documents(
381	        session,
382	        tenant_id,
383	        predecessor=original.document_id,
384	        successor=reversal.document_id,
385	        link_type=_REVERSES_LINK,
386	    )
387	
388	    await session.refresh(reversal)
389	    publish(
390	        session,
391	        JournalEntryReversed(
392	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
393	            entry_id=original.id,
394	            reversal_entry_id=reversal.id,
395	            reversal_entry_number=reversal.entry_number or "",
396	            document_type=original.document_type,
397	            reversal_date=reversal_date.isoformat(),
398	        ),
399	    )
400	    return reversal

1	"""D-015 exact money/quantity/rate representation on BOTH engines, plus allocation.
2	
3	The financial engine's DB-level invariants (the balance trigger, the one-side CHECK,
4	valuation math) are only meaningful if storage is EXACT on both backends. PostgreSQL has a
5	native NUMERIC; SQLite does not — ``sa.Numeric`` round-trips through float there and silently
6	loses precision. So each TypeDecorator stores NUMERIC on Postgres and an INTEGER of scaled
7	minor units on SQLite (value × 10^scale), converting to/from ``decimal.Decimal`` in the bind/
8	result processors. Trigger SQL therefore only ever SUMs and COMPARES the stored representation
9	(ints on SQLite, NUMERIC on PG) — never divides or scales — so the asymmetric storage stays
10	semantically identical where it matters (D-015 trigger discipline).
11	
12	Scales:
13	- ``MoneyType``      NUMERIC(18,6) / INTEGER micro-units (×10^6), scale 6 — headroom over the
14	  2/3 currency decimals so posting-time rounding has somewhere to live.
15	- ``QuantityType``   NUMERIC(18,6) / INTEGER micro-units (×10^6), scale 6 — UoM/FIFO math.
16	- ``RateType``       NUMERIC(20,10) / INTEGER nano-units (×10^10), scale 10 — FX rates keep
17	  full precision (rates are never quantized to currency decimals).
18	
19	Python is Decimal-only — never float. The TypeDecorators are ``cache_ok = True`` (they carry
20	no per-instance state beyond the fixed class scale), so SQLAlchemy may cache compiled
21	statements that use them.
22	
23	``allocate`` is the single largest-remainder splitter (D-015): tax/discount splits, payment
24	allocation, and the journal's functional-currency residual-cent balancing all route through it
25	so parts always sum EXACTLY to the total. ``quantize_money`` is the ROUND_HALF_UP boundary
26	rounding (commercial/SAP practice), keyed off a per-currency decimal-places lookup.
27	"""
28	
29	from __future__ import annotations
30	
31	from decimal import ROUND_DOWN, ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal
32	
33	import sqlalchemy as sa
34	from sqlalchemy.engine import Dialect
35	from sqlalchemy.types import TypeDecorator
36	
37	# Scales (number of fractional decimal digits each type stores).
38	_MONEY_SCALE = 6
39	_QUANTITY_SCALE = 6
40	_RATE_SCALE = 10
41	
42	
43	class _ScaledDecimalType(TypeDecorator[Decimal]):
44	    """Shared base for the three exact-decimal types (D-015).
45	
46	    ``impl`` is NUMERIC so the default (Postgres) rendering is a true decimal; on SQLite the
47	    column is loaded as INTEGER and the bind/result processors translate Decimal <-> scaled
48	    integer minor units. The conversion is exact in both directions because a Decimal with at
49	    most ``scale`` fractional digits maps to an integer with no rounding (values carrying more
50	    digits than the scale are quantized HALF_UP on the way in — money/quantities are quantized
51	    at their boundary before storage, so this only ever trims trailing noise)."""
52	
53	    # Required by TypeDecorator: the default (Postgres) decorated type. ``load_dialect_impl``
54	    # overrides it per dialect (BigInteger on SQLite, Numeric(precision, scale) on PG).
55	    impl = sa.Numeric
56	    cache_ok = True
57	
58	    # Concrete subclasses set these; the base is abstract by virtue of unset class attrs.
59	    scale: int
60	    precision: int
61	
62	    @property
63	    def python_type(self) -> type[Decimal]:
64	        return Decimal
65	
66	    def load_dialect_impl(self, dialect: Dialect) -> sa.types.TypeEngine[object]:
67	        if dialect.name == "sqlite":
68	            # Scaled minor units fit a 64-bit integer for the demo/test value ranges (D-015).
69	            return dialect.type_descriptor(sa.BigInteger())
70	        return dialect.type_descriptor(sa.Numeric(self.precision, self.scale))
71	
72	    @property
73	    def _quantum(self) -> Decimal:
74	        return Decimal(1).scaleb(-self.scale)
75	
76	    def process_bind_param(self, value: Decimal | int | str | None, dialect: Dialect):
77	        if value is None:
78	            return None
79	        as_decimal = value if isinstance(value, Decimal) else Decimal(str(value))
80	        if dialect.name == "sqlite":
81	            # Decimal -> integer scaled minor units. Quantize first so a value with more than
82	            # ``scale`` digits cannot leave a fractional remainder when multiplied out.
83	            scaled = as_decimal.quantize(self._quantum, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
84	            return int(scaled.scaleb(self.scale))
85	        return as_decimal
86	
87	    def process_result_value(self, value: int | Decimal | None, dialect: Dialect) -> Decimal | None:
88	        if value is None:
89	            return None
90	        if dialect.name == "sqlite":
91	            # Integer scaled minor units -> Decimal at the type's scale (exact, no float).
92	            return (Decimal(int(value)) * self._quantum).quantize(self._quantum)
93	        return value if isinstance(value, Decimal) else Decimal(str(value))
94	
95	
96	class MoneyType(_ScaledDecimalType):
97	    """Monetary amount (D-015): NUMERIC(18,6) on Postgres, INTEGER micro-units on SQLite."""
98	
99	    # cache_ok must be set on each concrete TypeDecorator class, not just the base.
100	    cache_ok = True
101	    scale = _MONEY_SCALE
102	    precision = 18
103	
104	
105	class QuantityType(_ScaledDecimalType):
106	    """Inventory quantity (D-015): NUMERIC(18,6) on Postgres, INTEGER micro-units on SQLite.
107	    Same storage as MoneyType but a distinct type so quantity and money columns read clearly."""
108	
109	    cache_ok = True
110	    scale = _QUANTITY_SCALE
111	    precision = 18
112	
113	
114	class RateType(_ScaledDecimalType):
115	    """FX/exchange rate (D-015): NUMERIC(20,10) on Postgres, INTEGER nano-units on SQLite.
116	    Scale 10 keeps full rate precision — rates are never quantized to currency decimals."""
117	
118	    cache_ok = True
119	    scale = _RATE_SCALE
120	    precision = 20
121	
122	
123	# --- Currency decimals + boundary rounding ------------------------------------
124	
125	# ISO 4217 fractional digits. Default is 2; non-2-decimal currencies are listed explicitly so
126	# the table can grow (JPY=0, BHD=3, ...). Stored journal amounts quantize to this at the
127	# posting/pricing boundary; unit prices/costs and FX rates keep full scale-6/10 precision.
128	_DEFAULT_CURRENCY_DECIMALS = 2
129	_CURRENCY_DECIMALS: dict[str, int] = {
130	    "JPY": 0,
131	    "KRW": 0,
132	    "BHD": 3,
133	    "KWD": 3,
134	    "OMR": 3,
135	    "TND": 3,
136	}
137	
138	
139	def currency_decimals(currency_code: str) -> int:
140	    """ISO 4217 fractional digits for ``currency_code`` (default 2). The amount-rounding
141	    boundary uses this so e.g. JPY rounds to whole units and BHD to three places (D-015)."""
142	    return _CURRENCY_DECIMALS.get(currency_code.upper(), _DEFAULT_CURRENCY_DECIMALS)
143	
144	
145	def quantize_money(value: Decimal, places: int = 2) -> Decimal:
146	    """Round ``value`` to ``places`` decimals HALF_UP (D-015 — commercial/SAP practice). Pass
147	    ``currency_decimals(code)`` for ``places`` to round to a currency's minor unit."""
148	    return value.quantize(Decimal(1).scaleb(-places), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
149	
150	
151	def quantize_for_currency(value: Decimal, currency_code: str) -> Decimal:
152	    """Round ``value`` to ``currency_code``'s minor unit HALF_UP (D-015)."""
153	    return quantize_money(value, currency_decimals(currency_code))
154	
155	
156	def allocate(total: Decimal, weights: list[Decimal], places: int = 2) -> list[Decimal]:
157	    """Split ``total`` across ``weights`` so the parts sum EXACTLY to ``total`` (D-015).
158	
159	    Largest-remainder method: each part is ``total × weight / Σweights`` rounded DOWN to
160	    ``places`` decimals, then the rounding residual (``total`` minus the sum of floored parts)
161	    is distributed one minor unit at a time to the parts with the largest fractional remainder,
162	    ties broken by original index. Deterministic, and the parts ALWAYS reconstitute the total —
163	    used for FX residual-cent absorption, tax splits, discount splits and payment allocation.
164	
165	    A zero or empty total returns zeros; zero total weight (all weights zero) splits ``total``
166	    evenly via equal unit weights so the result still sums to ``total`` rather than dropping it.
167	    """
168	    quantum = Decimal(1).scaleb(-places)
169	    n = len(weights)
170	    if n == 0:
171	        return []
172	    total_weight = sum(weights, Decimal(0))
173	    if total_weight == 0:
174	        # Degenerate: no weight to distribute by. Fall back to equal weights so the total is
175	        # still allocated exactly (never silently dropped).
176	        weights = [Decimal(1)] * n
177	        total_weight = Decimal(n)
178	
179	    exact = [total * weight / total_weight for weight in weights]
180	    floored = [part.quantize(quantum, rounding=ROUND_DOWN) for part in exact]
181	    remainders = [exact[i] - floored[i] for i in range(n)]
182	
183	    allocated = sum(floored, Decimal(0))
184	    residual = total - allocated
185	    # Number of whole minor units still to hand out (can be negative if total is negative).
186	    units = int((residual / quantum).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))
187	
188	    # Distribute to the largest remainders first; for a negative residual hand out negative
189	    # units to the SMALLEST remainders (those rounded least-down) so the result stays balanced.
190	    order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: (remainders[i], -i), reverse=units >= 0)
191	    step = quantum if units >= 0 else -quantum
192	    for k in range(abs(units)):
193	        floored[order[k % n]] += step
194	    return floored
195	
196	
197	__all__ = [
198	    "MoneyType",
199	    "QuantityType",
200	    "RateType",
201	    "allocate",
202	    "currency_decimals",
203	    "quantize_for_currency",
204	    "quantize_money",
205	]

1	"""Purpose-keyed account wiring (D-019), split out of service/fx.py to keep both under the cap.
2	
3	A ``PostingDefault`` maps a purpose string (e.g. ``'fx_unrealized_gain'``) to a GL account, so any
4	flow that must post to a CONFIGURED account resolves it data-driven rather than hard-coding an
5	account code. The FX engine is the first consumer (gain/loss + revaluation adjustment); AP/AR and
6	inventory COGS reuse the same mechanism in later phases. Kept a distinct concern file (not in
7	fx.py) because it is account wiring, not FX rate math.
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import uuid
13	
14	from sqlalchemy import select
15	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
16	
17	from app.core.exceptions import ValidationFailedError
18	from app.modules.finance.constants import FX_POSTING_PURPOSES
19	from app.modules.finance.models import Account, PostingDefault
20	
21	
22	async def get_posting_default(
23	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, purpose: str
24	) -> uuid.UUID:
25	    """Resolve a purpose string to its mapped account id (D-019). Raises a clear 422 when the
26	    purpose is unmapped — a flow that must post to a configured account (FX gain/loss, revaluation
27	    adjustment) fails loud rather than guessing. The data-driven account wiring reused later by
28	    AP/AR and inventory COGS."""
29	    account_id = (
30	        await session.execute(
31	            select(PostingDefault.account_id).where(
32	                PostingDefault.tenant_id == tenant_id, PostingDefault.purpose == purpose
33	            )
34	        )
35	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
36	    if account_id is None:
37	        raise ValidationFailedError(
38	            message=f"No account is mapped for posting purpose '{purpose}'",
39	            code="finance.posting_default_unmapped",
40	            details={"purpose": purpose},
41	        )
42	    return account_id
43	
44	
45	async def set_posting_default(
46	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, purpose: str, account_id: uuid.UUID
47	) -> PostingDefault:
48	    """Map (or remap) a purpose to an account (D-019). Validates the purpose is a known FX purpose
49	    and the account exists in the tenant + is postable; upserts the (tenant, purpose) row.
50	    Loaded-object mutation on remap so audit captures the change."""
51	    if purpose not in FX_POSTING_PURPOSES:
52	        raise ValidationFailedError(
53	            message=f"Unknown posting purpose '{purpose}'",
54	            code="finance.posting_default_unknown_purpose",
55	            details={"purpose": purpose},
56	        )
57	    account = (
58	        await session.execute(
59	            select(Account).where(Account.tenant_id == tenant_id, Account.id == account_id)
60	        )
61	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
62	    if account is None:
63	        raise ValidationFailedError(
64	            message="The mapped account does not exist in this tenant",
65	            code="finance.posting_default_account_not_found",
66	            details={"account_id": str(account_id)},
67	        )
68	    if not account.is_postable:
69	        raise ValidationFailedError(
70	            message="A posting default must map to a postable account",
71	            code="finance.posting_default_account_not_postable",
72	            details={"account_id": str(account_id)},
73	        )
74	    existing = (
75	        await session.execute(
76	            select(PostingDefault).where(
77	                PostingDefault.tenant_id == tenant_id, PostingDefault.purpose == purpose
78	            )
79	        )
80	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
81	    if existing is not None:
82	        existing.account_id = account_id
83	        await session.flush()
84	        return existing
85	    default = PostingDefault(tenant_id=tenant_id, purpose=purpose, account_id=account_id)
86	    session.add(default)
87	    await session.flush()
88	    return default
89	
90	
91	async def list_posting_defaults(
92	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID
93	) -> list[PostingDefault]:
94	    stmt = (
95	        select(PostingDefault)
96	        .where(PostingDefault.tenant_id == tenant_id)
97	        .order_by(PostingDefault.purpose)
98	    )
99	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())

3	The AP ``ap_router.py`` mirror. Split out of router.py (at the STRUCTURE §3 400-line cap) the same
4	way fx_router/tax_router/ap_router are: mounted via ``router.include_router(ar_router)`` so the
5	module stays ONE surface at ``/api/v1/finance`` — no second mount in main.py. Reads are guarded by

7	``finance.ar.collect`` (D-009). Writes commit through ``run_in_uow`` (D-011) so audit + events ride
8	the transaction; the financial-document endpoints (post invoice, create receipt) and the dunning run

170	    "/customer-receipts",

172	    status_code=201,
173	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(FINANCE_AR_COLLECT))],
174	)
175	async def create_customer_receipt(
176	    payload: CustomerReceiptCreate,
177	    current: CurrentUserDep,
178	    session: SessionDep,
179	    idem: IdempotentDep = _ReceiptIdempotentDep,
180	) -> CustomerReceiptDetail:
181	    """Create + post a customer receipt clearing open invoices (PLAN 4.6). IDEMPOTENT (D-013): it
182	    posts a journal entry + clears open items, so a retried request must not double-receive."""
183	    holder: dict[str, CustomerReceiptDetail] = {}
184	
185	    async def work() -> None:
186	        receipt = await service.create_and_post_receipt(session, current.tenant_id, payload)
187	        detail = await _receipt_detail(session, current.tenant_id, receipt.id)
188	        holder["read"] = await idem.capture(detail, status_code=201)
189	
190	    await run_in_uow(session, work)
191	    return holder["read"]
192	
193	
194	@ar_router.get(
195	    "/customer-receipts",
196	    response_model=Page[CustomerReceiptRead],
197	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(FINANCE_AR_READ))],
198	)
199	async def list_customer_receipts(
200	    current: CurrentUserDep,
201	    session: SessionDep,
202	    params: CursorParams = CursorParamsDep,
203	    partner_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
204	) -> Page[CustomerReceiptRead]:
205	    page = await service.list_customer_receipts(
206	        session,
207	        current.tenant_id,
208	        cursor=params.cursor,
209	        limit=params.limit,
210	        partner_id=partner_id,
211	    )
212	    return Page(
213	        items=[CustomerReceiptRead.model_validate(item) for item in page.items],
214	        next_cursor=page.next_cursor,
215	        limit=page.limit,
216	    )
217	
218	
219	# --- Dunning ------------------------------------------------------------------
220	
221	
222	@ar_router.post(
223	    "/dunning-runs",
224	    response_model=DunningRunResult,
225	    status_code=201,
226	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(FINANCE_AR_COLLECT))],
227	)
228	async def run_dunning(
229	    payload: DunningRunRequest,
230	    current: CurrentUserDep,
231	    session: SessionDep,
232	    idem: IdempotentDep = _DunningIdempotentDep,
233	) -> DunningRunResult:
234	    """Run a dunning pass (PLAN 4.6): advance the reminder level on overdue open invoices and return
235	    the notice list. Posts no journal. IDEMPOTENT (D-013) and idempotent-ish per day (a re-run the
236	    same ``as_of`` advances nothing already at its earned level)."""
237	    holder: dict[str, DunningRunResult] = {}
238	
239	    async def work() -> None:
240	        run = await service.run_dunning(
241	            session, current.tenant_id, payload.as_of, payload.partner_id
242	        )
243	        result = DunningRunResult.model_validate(run)
244	        holder["read"] = await idem.capture(result, status_code=201)
245	
246	    await run_in_uow(session, work)
247	    return holder["read"]

251	
252

254	    "/ar-aging",
255	    response_model=ArAgingReportRead,
256	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(FINANCE_AR_READ))],
257	)

263	) -> ArAgingReportRead:
264	    """AR aging as of ``as_of`` (PLAN 4.6): per-partner buckets + totals over open invoices."""
265	    report = await service.customer_aging(session, current.tenant_id, as_of, partner_id)

1	"""Multi-currency master data + posting-default wiring (D-019).
2	
3	Four tables, the third file in the finance ``models/`` package (STRUCTURE §3):
4	
5	- ``Currency`` (``fin_currencies``): the tenant's currency catalog. Exactly one row per tenant
6	  is the FUNCTIONAL currency (the books' reporting currency); the one-functional invariant is
7	  enforced by the service (``service/fx.set_functional_currency``) and the partial unique index
8	  declared below backstops it at the DB on both engines.
9	- ``ExchangeRate`` (``fin_exchange_rates``): a rate for a (from, to, rate_type) pair on a date.
10	  ``get_rate`` picks the most recent rate with ``rate_date <= on_date`` (D-019: postings never
11	  guess — a missing rate is a hard 422). ``rate`` is ``RateType`` (NUMERIC(20,10) / nano-unit
12	  ints, D-015) so rates keep full precision and are never quantized to currency decimals.
13	- ``PostingDefault`` (``fin_posting_defaults``): purpose-keyed account wiring (D-019). One row
14	  per (tenant, purpose) maps a purpose string (e.g. ``'fx_unrealized_gain'``) to an account, so
15	  the FX engine — and later AP/AR/inventory COGS — resolve accounts data-driven rather than
16	  hard-coded.
17	- ``FxRevaluationRun`` (``fin_fx_revaluation_runs``): bookkeeping for one unrealized-FX
18	  revaluation run (D-019). Tracks the run's period, rate_date and status; its posted entries are
19	  linked via docflow (``'revalues'`` edges) so a re-run can reverse exactly the prior run's
20	  entries (append-only, never delete).
21	
22	All four follow the D-007 composite-tenant-FK backstop. Enum-valued columns are plain
23	``sa.String`` storing the StrEnum value (matching the rest of finance); the service maps
24	to/from the constants classes.
25	"""
26	
27	import uuid
28	from datetime import date
29	
30	import sqlalchemy as sa
31	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
32	
33	from app.core.models import (
34	    AuditMixin,
35	    Base,
36	    TenantMixin,
37	    TimestampMixin,
38	    UuidPKMixin,
39	    tenant_fk,
40	    tenant_unique,
41	)
42	from app.core.money import RateType
43	from app.modules.finance.constants import FxRunStatus, RateKind
44	
45	
46	class Currency(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
47	    """A currency in the tenant's catalog (D-019). ``code`` is the ISO-4217 alpha code
48	    (e.g. ``'USD'``); ``decimal_places`` is the minor-unit scale used to quantize posting
49	    amounts (default 2; JPY=0, BHD=3). Exactly one currency per tenant has ``is_functional``
50	    TRUE — the books' reporting currency. Audited (D-010): currency config is master data."""
51	
52	    __tablename__ = "fin_currencies"
53	    __table_args__ = (
54	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "code", name="uq_fin_currencies_tenant_id_code"),
55	        tenant_unique(),
56	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
57	    )
58	
59	    code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(3), nullable=False)
60	    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(100), nullable=False)
61	    decimal_places: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
62	        sa.Integer, nullable=False, default=2, server_default="2"
63	    )
64	    is_functional: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
65	        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=False, server_default=sa.false()
66	    )
67	
68	
69	class ExchangeRate(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
70	    """One exchange rate (D-019). A (tenant, rate_date, from, to, rate_type) row gives the
71	    ``rate`` to multiply a ``from_currency_code`` amount by to get ``to_currency_code``.
72	    ``rate_type`` is SPOT (posting-time translation) or CLOSING (period-end revaluation).
73	    Audited (D-010): rate edits change historical translation if mis-dated, so they are
74	    tracked."""
75	
76	    __tablename__ = "fin_exchange_rates"
77	    __table_args__ = (
78	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
79	            "tenant_id",
80	            "rate_date",
81	            "from_currency_code",
82	            "to_currency_code",
83	            "rate_type",
84	            name="uq_fin_exchange_rates_pair",
85	        ),
86	        tenant_unique(),
87	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
88	        # The hot lookup get_rate runs on every foreign-currency posting: the most recent rate
89	        # for a (pair, type) with rate_date <= on_date.
90	        sa.Index(
91	            "ix_fin_exchange_rates_lookup",
92	            "tenant_id",
93	            "from_currency_code",
94	            "to_currency_code",
95	            "rate_type",
96	            "rate_date",
97	        ),
98	    )
99	
100	    rate_date: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=False)
101	    from_currency_code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(3), nullable=False)
102	    to_currency_code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(3), nullable=False)
103	    rate_type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
104	        sa.String(10), nullable=False, default=RateKind.SPOT.value, server_default="SPOT"
105	    )
106	    rate: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(RateType(), nullable=False)
107	
108	
109	class PostingDefault(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
110	    """Purpose-keyed account wiring (D-019). One row per (tenant, purpose) maps a purpose
111	    string to a GL account, so flows that must post to a configured account (FX gain/loss,
112	    revaluation adjustment, later AP/AR/COGS) resolve it data-driven via
113	    ``service/fx.get_posting_default``. Composite tenant FK to fin_accounts. Audited (D-010):
114	    account wiring is configuration that changes where money lands."""
115	
116	    __tablename__ = "fin_posting_defaults"
117	    __table_args__ = (
118	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
119	            "tenant_id", "purpose", name="uq_fin_posting_defaults_tenant_id_purpose"
120	        ),
121	        tenant_unique(),
122	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
123	        tenant_fk("fin_accounts", "account_id"),
124	    )
125	
126	    purpose: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=False)
127	    account_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
128	
129	
130	class FxRevaluationRun(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
131	    """Bookkeeping for one unrealized-FX revaluation run (D-019). ``fiscal_period_id`` is the
132	    period being revalued (composite tenant FK); ``rate_date`` is the CLOSING-rate date (the
133	    period end). ``status`` is DRAFT->COMPLETED while running, or REVERSED once a later run has
134	    reversed this run's entries. The run's posted FX_REVAL entries are linked via docflow
135	    (``'revalues'`` edges) so a re-run reverses exactly the prior run's entries — append-only,
136	    never delete. Audited (D-010): a revaluation run posts to the GL."""
137	
138	    __tablename__ = "fin_fx_revaluation_runs"
139	    __table_args__ = (
140	        tenant_unique(),
141	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
142	        tenant_fk("fin_fiscal_periods", "fiscal_period_id"),
143	    )
144	
145	    fiscal_period_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
146	    rate_date: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=False)
147	    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
148	        sa.String(12),
149	        nullable=False,
150	        default=FxRunStatus.COMPLETED.value,
151	        server_default="COMPLETED",
152	    )
153	
154	
155	# One functional currency per tenant (D-019): a partial unique index on (tenant_id) WHERE
156	# is_functional, so a second functional currency is rejected at the DB on both engines. Declared
157	# outside the class so the predicate is a column expression (the D-007 grep gate bans raw-SQL
158	# under app/modules/); both dialect kwargs are required (each engine needs its own predicate).
159	sa.Index(
160	    "uq_fin_currencies_one_functional",
161	    Currency.tenant_id,
162	    unique=True,
163	    postgresql_where=Currency.is_functional,
164	    sqlite_where=Currency.is_functional,
165	)

1	"""D-012 gapless per-tenant document numbering.
2	
3	One half of the merged registry+numbering subsystem (the other half is core/docflow.py).
4	A document number is claimed INSIDE the business transaction that makes the document
5	permanent (drafts are numbered at posting). Because the counter increment and the
6	document insert commit or roll back together, gaplessness for committed documents falls
7	out of ACID with no burned-number reconciliation state (D-012 claim-timing rule).
8	
9	The atomic claim is a single ``UPDATE core_number_sequences SET next_value = next_value + 1
10	... RETURNING next_value`` — one portable statement that takes the row lock and reads the
11	new counter in one round trip. RETURNING is verified working on the project's aiosqlite
12	(SQLite >= 3.35; this build runs 3.53) and on Postgres, so no SELECT-then-UPDATE fallback
13	is needed (D-012 sanctioned the fallback only if RETURNING were unavailable).
14	
15	The ORM model lives HERE rather than in core/models.py: models.py is at ~273 lines and
16	adding the numbering + docflow entities would push it over the ~350-line soft cap, so the
17	D-012 entities sit in their concern files (numbering.py / docflow.py) — a placement the
18	PLAN sanctions explicitly and STRUCTURE §2 permits ("one concept per file": the sequence
19	concept lives with its claim logic). Noted in DECISIONS.md.
20	"""
21	
22	import uuid
23	from datetime import date
24	
25	import sqlalchemy as sa
26	from sqlalchemy import select
27	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
28	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
29	
30	from app.core.exceptions import NotFoundError
31	from app.core.models import (
32	    Base,
33	    TenantMixin,
34	    TimestampMixin,
35	    UuidPKMixin,
36	    tenant_fk,
37	)

40	class NumberSequence(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
41	    """Per-tenant gapless counter for one document kind (D-012).
42	
43	    ``name`` is the namespaced sequence key (e.g. ``'finance.invoice'``); a claim formats
44	    ``{prefix}-{year?}-{padded next_value}`` (e.g. ``INV-2026-00001``). When ``year_reset``
45	    is set the running number restarts at 1 each calendar year and the year segment is
46	    rendered; ``current_year`` records which year the counter currently belongs to so the
47	    first claim of a new year resets it on demand (no rollover job, per D-012). Not
48	    AuditMixin: sequence rows are infrastructure counters mutated on every claim, not
49	    business state — auditing every increment would be noise (documented exclusion)."""
50	
51	    __tablename__ = "core_number_sequences"
52	    __table_args__ = (
53	        # One sequence per (tenant, name). Explicit name: the D-022 convention keys on
54	        # column 0 (tenant_id) only and would collide with tenant_unique() below.
55	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "name", name="uq_core_number_sequences_tenant_id_name"),
56	        # UNIQUE(tenant_id, id) so other tenant-scoped tables could reference a sequence via
57	        # the composite-FK backstop if ever needed (D-007 item 4).
58	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "id", name="uq_core_number_sequences_tenant_id"),
59	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
60	    )
61	
62	    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(100), nullable=False)
63	    prefix: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(20), nullable=False)
64	    padding: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=False)
65	    # Next number to hand out. The atomic claim does next_value = next_value + 1 RETURNING
66	    # the post-increment value, so the FIRST claim of a sequence at next_value=1 returns 1.
67	    next_value: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
68	        sa.Integer, nullable=False, default=1, server_default=sa.text("1")
69	    )
70	    year_reset: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
71	        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=False, server_default=sa.false()
72	    )
73	    # The year the running counter belongs to (NULL when year_reset is off).
74	    current_year: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=True)
75	
76	
77	def _format_number(prefix: str, padding: int, value: int, year: int | None) -> str:
78	    """Render ``{prefix}-{year?}-{padded value}`` — the year segment is present only when
79	    the sequence year-resets (D-012). e.g. ('INV', 5, 1, 2026) -> 'INV-2026-00001'."""
80	    padded = str(value).zfill(padding)
81	    if year is None:
82	        return f"{prefix}-{padded}"
83	    return f"{prefix}-{year}-{padded}"

86	async def ensure_sequence(
87	    session: AsyncSession,
88	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
89	    name: str,
90	    prefix: str,
91	    padding: int,
92	    year_reset: bool,
93	) -> NumberSequence:
94	    """Idempotent creator for provisioning/seed (D-012: year rollover and sequence setup
95	    need no job — the row is created on demand). Returns the existing row unchanged if the
96	    (tenant, name) sequence already exists, otherwise inserts it at next_value=1.
97	
98	    A Core insert is used (not an ORM add) so the tenant_id is set explicitly and the row
99	    is not subject to ORM tenant stamping — consistent with the D-007 sanction that core/
100	    numbering writes carry tenant_id explicitly. Callers run under the target tenant context
101	    or system_context (provisioning)."""
102	    existing = (
103	        await session.execute(
104	            select(NumberSequence).where(
105	                NumberSequence.tenant_id == tenant_id, NumberSequence.name == name
106	            )
107	        )
108	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
109	    if existing is not None:
110	        return existing
111	
112	    current_year = date.today().year if year_reset else None
113	    await session.execute(
114	        sa.insert(NumberSequence.__table__).values(
115	            id=uuid.uuid4(),
116	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
117	            name=name,
118	            prefix=prefix,
119	            padding=padding,
120	            next_value=1,
121	            year_reset=year_reset,
122	            current_year=current_year,
123	        )
124	    )
125	    return (
126	        await session.execute(
127	            select(NumberSequence).where(
128	                NumberSequence.tenant_id == tenant_id, NumberSequence.name == name
129	            )
130	        )
131	    ).scalar_one()
132	
133	
134	async def claim_number(
135	    session: AsyncSession,
136	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
137	    sequence_name: str,
138	    *,
139	    on_date: date,
140	) -> str:
141	    """Atomically claim the next number for ``sequence_name`` and return the formatted
142	    string (D-012). The claim runs in the CALLER's transaction — the number is permanent
143	    only when that transaction commits, so a rollback returns the value to the pool and the
144	    next committed claim reuses it (gaplessness for committed documents).
145	
146	    Mechanism — one portable atomic statement per claim:
147	    ``UPDATE core_number_sequences SET next_value = next_value + 1
148	      WHERE tenant_id=:t AND name=:n RETURNING next_value`` — the RETURNING value is the
149	    post-increment counter; the row lock the UPDATE takes serializes concurrent claimers so
150	    two claims can never read the same number (verified on aiosqlite >= 3.35 and Postgres).
151	
152	    Year reset (when ``year_reset``): if ``on_date.year`` differs from the stored
153	    ``current_year``, the counter is reset to 1 for the new year FIRST (a guarded UPDATE
154	    that only fires while current_year is still the old value, so a concurrent claimer that
155	    reset it already cannot double-reset), then the normal atomic increment claims 1.
156	
157	    A Core UPDATE is used (bypasses the ORM tenant filter by design — core/ numbering is a
158	    D-007 sanctioned raw-SQL site with explicit tenant_id)."""
159	    sequence = (
160	        await session.execute(
161	            select(NumberSequence).where(
162	                NumberSequence.tenant_id == tenant_id, NumberSequence.name == sequence_name
163	            )
164	        )
165	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
166	    if sequence is None:
167	        raise NotFoundError(
168	            message=f"Number sequence '{sequence_name}' is not configured for this tenant",
169	            code="core.number_sequence_missing",
170	        )
171	
172	    table = NumberSequence.__table__
173	    claim_year: int | None = None
174	    if sequence.year_reset:
175	        claim_year = on_date.year
176	        if sequence.current_year != claim_year:
177	            # Reset to 1 for the new year, guarded on the OLD current_year so a racing
178	            # claimer that already rolled the year over does not reset a second time.
179	            await session.execute(
180	                sa.update(table)
181	                .where(
182	                    table.c.tenant_id == tenant_id,
183	                    table.c.name == sequence_name,
184	                    table.c.current_year.is_not_distinct_from(sequence.current_year),
185	                )
186	                .values(next_value=1, current_year=claim_year)
187	            )
188	
189	    result = await session.execute(
190	        sa.update(table)
191	        .where(table.c.tenant_id == tenant_id, table.c.name == sequence_name)
192	        .values(next_value=table.c.next_value + 1)
193	        .returning(table.c.next_value)
194	    )
195	    next_after = result.scalar_one()
196	    claimed_value = next_after - 1
197	
198	    # The Core UPDATE changed the row out from under the loaded ORM object; expire it so its
199	    # attributes reload from the DB on next access rather than being marked dirty (which
200	    # would trigger a redundant ORM UPDATE on the next flush).
201	    formatted = _format_number(sequence.prefix, sequence.padding, claimed_value, claim_year)
202	    session.expire(sequence)
203	    return formatted

1	"""D-012 document registry, flow links, and chain traversal.
2	
3	The registry turns the polymorphic (doc_type, doc_id) problem into ordinary FK integrity:
4	every business document row links to exactly one ``core_documents`` registry entry via the
5	NOT NULL ``document_id`` FK supplied by ``DocumentMixin``. Predecessor/successor edges live
6	in ``core_doc_links``, so chain traversal is one generic recursive CTE over two narrow
7	tables — the ACDOCA-era Document Relationship Browser shape — with zero module-aware code in
8	core (core imports nothing from modules).
9	
10	Claim-timing (D-012): a document is registered with ``doc_number`` NULL at creation;
11	documents with a draft lifecycle are numbered at posting via the numbering claim, documents
12	permanent at creation are numbered immediately. The partial unique index on
13	``(tenant_id, doc_number)`` is the DB backstop turning any numbering bug into a constraint
14	violation.
15	
16	The ORM models live HERE rather than in core/models.py: models.py is near its ~350-line
17	soft cap, so the D-012 entities sit in their concern file (consistent with numbering.py and
18	sanctioned by the PLAN). Noted in DECISIONS.md.
19	"""
20	
21	import uuid
22	from dataclasses import dataclass
23	
24	import sqlalchemy as sa
25	from sqlalchemy import select
26	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
27	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, declared_attr, mapped_column
28	
29	from app.core.models import (
30	    Base,
31	    TenantMixin,
32	    TimestampMixin,
33	    UuidPKMixin,
34	    tenant_fk,
35	)
36	
37	# Depth ceiling on chain traversal (D-012): real chains are <10 nodes; the cap plus the
38	# visited-path cycle guard make a malformed graph terminate instead of spinning.
39	_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH = 20

41	
42	class Document(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
43	    """Registry entry for one business document (D-012). ``doc_type`` is a namespaced
44	    constant (``'sales.order'``, ``'finance.journal_entry'``) declared in module
45	    constants.py; ``doc_id`` is the PK of the business row in its own table; ``doc_number``
46	    is assigned at posting (NULL until then); ``status`` is the registry-level status string.
47	
48	    Not AuditMixin: the registry mirrors business rows that are themselves audited — the
49	    document's own table carries the audited business state, so auditing the registry too
50	    would double-record (documented exclusion)."""
51	
52	    __tablename__ = "core_documents"
53	    __table_args__ = (
54	        # One registry row per business document. Explicit name (D-022 convention keys on
55	        # column 0 only and would collide with tenant_unique()).
56	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
57	            "tenant_id", "doc_type", "doc_id", name="uq_core_documents_tenant_id_doc_type_doc_id"
58	        ),
59	        # Required so business rows can reference a registry entry via the composite tenant FK
60	        # (D-007 item 4) — DocumentMixin.document_fk() targets this.
61	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "id", name="uq_core_documents_tenant_id"),
62	        # Partial unique index: a tenant may have many UNNUMBERED documents (doc_number NULL)
63	        # but never two with the SAME doc_number. Both dialect kwargs are required — Postgres
64	        # and SQLite each need their own (D-012 / D-021 dialect-kwargs pattern); a plain
65	        # UNIQUE would (incorrectly) reject multiple NULLs on some engines.
66	        sa.Index(
67	            "uq_core_documents_tenant_id_doc_number",
68	            "tenant_id",
69	            "doc_number",
70	            unique=True,
71	            postgresql_where=sa.text("doc_number IS NOT NULL"),
72	            sqlite_where=sa.text("doc_number IS NOT NULL"),
73	        ),
74	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
75	    )

78	    doc_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
79	    doc_number: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=True)
80	    status: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(40), nullable=True)

83	class DocumentLink(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
84	    """A predecessor -> successor edge between two registry entries (D-012). ``link_type``
85	    names the relationship (``'fulfills'``, ``'invoices'``, ``'reverses'``, ``'posts'``).
86	    Both endpoints carry the composite tenant FK backstop so an edge can never span tenants.
87	    A CHECK forbids self-edges (a document cannot be its own predecessor)."""
88	
89	    __tablename__ = "core_doc_links"
90	    __table_args__ = (
91	        # One edge per (tenant, predecessor, successor). Explicit name (D-022 column-0 rule).
92	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
93	            "tenant_id",
94	            "predecessor_document_id",
95	            "successor_document_id",
96	            name="uq_core_doc_links_tenant_id_predecessor_document_id_successor",
97	        ),

100	        # ck_<table>_<constraint_name> -> ck_core_doc_links_no_self_link (matches 0006).
101	        sa.CheckConstraint(
102	            "predecessor_document_id != successor_document_id",
103	            name="no_self_link",
104	        ),

106	        # Both endpoints reference core_documents through the composite tenant FK, so the
107	        # D-022 column-0 convention would name both identically (collision). Spell out
108	        # distinct names that match migration 0006 exactly.

110	            ["tenant_id", "predecessor_document_id"],
111	            ["core_documents.tenant_id", "core_documents.id"],
112	            name="fk_core_doc_links_tenant_id_core_documents",
113	        ),
114	        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
115	            ["tenant_id", "successor_document_id"],
116	            ["core_documents.tenant_id", "core_documents.id"],
117	            name="fk_core_doc_links_successor_document_id_core_documents",
118	        ),
119	    )

121	    predecessor_document_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
122	    successor_document_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
123	    link_type: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(40), nullable=True)

126	def document_fk() -> sa.ForeignKeyConstraint:
127	    """Composite tenant-safe FK for a business table's ``document_id`` -> core_documents
128	    (D-007 item 4). A business model that mixes in DocumentMixin adds this to its
129	    __table_args__ so the link can never point at another tenant's registry row, mirroring
130	    the tenant_fk()/tenant_unique() pattern in core/models.py."""
131	    return sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
132	        ["tenant_id", "document_id"],
133	        ["core_documents.tenant_id", "core_documents.id"],
134	    )

137	class DocumentMixin:
138	    """Business-document link mixin (D-012). A business model mixes this in to get a NOT NULL
139	    ``document_id`` column tying its row to its registry entry — so the row CANNOT be inserted
140	    without first registering the document (the dual-write discipline D-012 relies on). The
141	    consuming model must also add ``document_fk()`` to its __table_args__ for the composite
142	    tenant-safe FK (a mixin cannot inject a multi-column FK into the host's __table_args__,
143	    exactly as TenantMixin needs the model to add tenant_fk()). UNIQUE so the registry-to-row
144	    mapping is 1:1.
145	
146	    Usage in a later module model:
147	
148	        class SalesOrder(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, DocumentMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
149	            __tablename__ = "sls_orders"
150	            __table_args__ = (tenant_unique(), tenant_fk("adm_tenants"), document_fk())
151	    """

153	    @declared_attr
154	    def document_id(cls) -> Mapped[uuid.UUID]:
155	        return mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False, unique=True)

187	async def register_document(
188	    session: AsyncSession,
189	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
190	    doc_type: str,
191	    doc_id: uuid.UUID,
192	    *,
193	    doc_number: str | None = None,
194	    status: str | None = None,
195	) -> Document:
196	    """Insert a registry row for a business document and return it (D-012). Called by the
197	    creating service in the same transaction as the business-row insert (the DocumentMixin
198	    NOT NULL FK makes skipping it a hard error). ``doc_number`` is left NULL for draft-
199	    lifecycle documents (numbered later at posting) and set for documents permanent at
200	    creation. A Core insert sets tenant_id explicitly — core/docflow is a D-007 sanctioned
201	    raw-SQL site."""
202	    document_id = uuid.uuid4()
203	    await session.execute(
204	        sa.insert(Document.__table__).values(
205	            id=document_id,
206	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
207	            doc_type=doc_type,
208	            doc_id=doc_id,

218	async def set_document_status(
219	    session: AsyncSession,
220	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
221	    document_id: uuid.UUID,
222	    *,
223	    status: str | None = None,
224	    doc_number: str | None = None,
225	) -> None:
226	    """Update a registry row's status and/or doc_number in the owning transaction (D-012).
227	
228	    The number is assigned at the moment a draft-lifecycle document becomes permanent (journal
229	    posting) — passing ``doc_number`` here writes it through the partial-unique (tenant,
230	    doc_number) backstop, so any numbering bug surfaces as a constraint violation. Only the
231	    provided arguments are changed (``None`` leaves the column untouched, except doc_number which
232	    is always set when supplied). A Core UPDATE addressed by (tenant_id, id) — a D-007 sanctioned
233	    explicit-tenant raw-SQL site."""
234	    values: dict[str, str | None] = {}
235	    if status is not None:
236	        values["status"] = status
237	    if doc_number is not None:
238	        values["doc_number"] = doc_number
239	    if not values:
240	        return
241	    await session.execute(
242	        sa.update(Document.__table__)
243	        .where(
244	            Document.__table__.c.tenant_id == tenant_id,
245	            Document.__table__.c.id == document_id,
246	        )
247	        .values(**values)

251	async def link_documents(
252	    session: AsyncSession,
253	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
254	    predecessor: uuid.UUID,
255	    successor: uuid.UUID,
256	    link_type: str | None = None,
257	) -> DocumentLink:
258	    """Create a predecessor -> successor edge and return it (D-012). The UNIQUE(tenant_id,
259	    predecessor, successor) constraint rejects a duplicate edge as an IntegrityError, and
260	    the composite tenant FKs reject endpoints from another tenant. A Core insert sets
261	    tenant_id explicitly (D-007 sanctioned site)."""
262	    link_id = uuid.uuid4()
263	    await session.execute(
264	        sa.insert(DocumentLink.__table__).values(
265	            id=link_id,
266	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
267	            predecessor_document_id=predecessor,
268	            successor_document_id=successor,
269	            link_type=link_type,
270	        )
271	    )
272	    return (
273	        await session.execute(select(DocumentLink).where(DocumentLink.id == link_id))
274	    ).scalar_one()

276	
277	def _build_reachability_cte(
278	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID, start: uuid.UUID, *, forward: bool
279	) -> sa.sql.Selectable:
280	    """One recursive CTE collecting every document reachable from ``start`` in ONE direction.
281	
282	    ``forward=True`` walks successor edges (descendants), ``forward=False`` walks predecessor
283	    edges (ancestors). The recursive member carries a ``depth`` column capped at
284	    _MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH and a ``path`` string of visited ids; the join excludes any node already
285	    on the path, so a diamond or cycle is traversed once and terminates (D-012 visited-path
286	    guard). Works identically on Postgres and SQLite (both support WITH RECURSIVE).
287	    """
288	    links = DocumentLink.__table__
289	    near = links.c.successor_document_id if forward else links.c.predecessor_document_id
290	    far = links.c.predecessor_document_id if forward else links.c.successor_document_id
291	
292	    # Anchor: the start node itself at depth 0. The path representation MUST match how the
293	    # recursive step casts ids (CAST(<Uuid column> AS VARCHAR)), so the start id is cast the
294	    # same way — casting a Uuid-typed literal renders dashless hex on SQLite and dashed on
295	    # PG, exactly as the column cast does, keeping the visited-path guard's LIKE comparison
296	    # apples-to-apples on both engines (a raw str(start) would carry dashes on SQLite and
297	    # silently defeat the guard).
298	    anchor = select(
299	        sa.literal(start, type_=sa.Uuid).label("document_id"),
300	        sa.literal(0).label("depth"),
301	        sa.cast(sa.literal(start, type_=sa.Uuid), sa.String).label("path"),
302	    ).cte("reach", recursive=True)
303	
304	    # Recursive step: from each frontier node, follow edges in the chosen direction to the
305	    # node on the other end, within the tenant, skipping nodes already on the path.
306	    step = (
307	        select(
308	            far.label("document_id"),
309	            (anchor.c.depth + 1).label("depth"),
310	            (anchor.c.path + sa.literal(",") + sa.cast(far, sa.String)).label("path"),
311	        )
312	        .select_from(anchor.join(links, near == anchor.c.document_id))
313	        .where(
314	            links.c.tenant_id == tenant_id,
315	            anchor.c.depth < _MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH,
316	            anchor.c.path.notlike(sa.literal("%") + sa.cast(far, sa.String) + sa.literal("%")),
317	        )
318	    )
319	    return anchor.union_all(step)
320	
321	
322	async def get_document_chain(
323	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, document_id: uuid.UUID
324	) -> DocumentChain:
325	    """Traverse the full flow chain around ``document_id`` in BOTH directions and return its
326	    nodes + edges (D-012). Two recursive CTEs (ancestors via predecessor edges, descendants
327	    via successor edges) collect every reachable registry id; their union is the connected
328	    component containing the start node. Edges are the links whose BOTH endpoints fall in that
329	    set. Cycles and diamonds are handled by the per-CTE visited-path guard, so each node and
330	    edge appears once. Returns empty nodes/edges when the id is unknown to this tenant.
331	
332	    Tenant isolation: the CTEs filter links by tenant_id and the registry/edge reads run
333	    under the caller's tenant context (the D-007 ORM filter), so a chain query never returns
334	    another tenant's documents.
335	    """
336	    ancestors = _build_reachability_cte(tenant_id, document_id, forward=False)
337	    descendants = _build_reachability_cte(tenant_id, document_id, forward=True)
338	
339	    ancestor_ids = set(
340	        (await session.execute(select(ancestors.c.document_id))).scalars().all()
341	    )
342	    descendant_ids = set(
343	        (await session.execute(select(descendants.c.document_id))).scalars().all()
344	    )
345	    reachable = ancestor_ids | descendant_ids
346	
347	    # An unknown id reaches only itself; if it is not a real registry row for this tenant,
348	    # there are no nodes to return — surface an empty chain (the router maps that to 404).
349	    document_rows = (
350	        await session.execute(select(Document).where(Document.id.in_(reachable)))
351	    ).scalars().all()
352	    if not document_rows:
353	        return DocumentChain(nodes=[], edges=[])
354	
355	    present_ids = {row.id for row in document_rows}
356	    nodes = [
357	        ChainNode(
358	            document_id=row.id,
359	            doc_type=row.doc_type,
360	            doc_id=row.doc_id,
361	            doc_number=row.doc_number,
362	            status=row.status,
363	        )
364	        for row in document_rows
365	    ]
366	
367	    link_rows = (
368	        await session.execute(
369	            select(DocumentLink).where(
370	                DocumentLink.predecessor_document_id.in_(present_ids),
371	                DocumentLink.successor_document_id.in_(present_ids),
372	            )
373	        )
374	    ).scalars().all()
375	    edges = [
376	        ChainEdge(
377	            predecessor_document_id=link.predecessor_document_id,
378	            successor_document_id=link.successor_document_id,
379	            link_type=link.link_type,
380	        )
381	        for link in link_rows
382	    ]
383	
384	    return DocumentChain(nodes=nodes, edges=edges)

1	"""Journal read surface (D-017/D-021): entry/line loaders + the paginated list.
2	
3	Split out of ``service/journal.py`` so the write engine (create/post/reverse) stays under the
4	STRUCTURE §3 400-line cap; both halves are the one journal aggregate. The write engine imports the
5	loaders from here; the router imports the read functions through the ``service`` package surface.
6	"""
7	
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import uuid
11	from decimal import Decimal
12	
13	from sqlalchemy import select
14	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
15	
16	from app.core.exceptions import NotFoundError
17	from app.core.pagination import OrderKey, SortDirection, filter_fingerprint, paginate
18	from app.core.schemas import Page
19	from app.modules.finance.constants import EntryStatus
20	from app.modules.finance.models import JournalEntry, JournalLine
21	
22	
23	async def load_lines(
24	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, entry_id: uuid.UUID
25	) -> list[JournalLine]:
26	    """Lines of an entry ordered by line_number (the order posting/reversal iterate in)."""
27	    stmt = (
28	        select(JournalLine)
29	        .where(
30	            JournalLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
31	            JournalLine.journal_entry_id == entry_id,
32	        )
33	        .order_by(JournalLine.line_number)
34	    )
35	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())
36	
37	
38	async def get_entry(
39	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, entry_id: uuid.UUID
40	) -> JournalEntry:
41	    entry = await session.get(JournalEntry, entry_id)
42	    if entry is None or entry.tenant_id != tenant_id:
43	        raise NotFoundError(
44	            message="Journal entry not found", code="finance.journal_entry_not_found"
45	        )
46	    return entry
47	
48	
49	async def get_entry_with_lines(
50	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, entry_id: uuid.UUID
51	) -> tuple[JournalEntry, list[JournalLine]]:
52	    """The entry plus its ordered lines (the GET /{id} and post/reverse response shape). 404 if
53	    the entry is unknown to this tenant."""
54	    entry = await get_entry(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
55	    lines = await load_lines(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
56	    return entry, lines
57	
58	
59	def entry_totals(lines: list[JournalLine]) -> tuple[Decimal, Decimal]:
60	    """(total functional debit, total functional credit) over the lines — the balance check
61	    operand. MoneyType result values are Decimal, so the sum is exact (D-015)."""
62	    debit = sum((line.functional_debit_amount for line in lines), Decimal(0))
63	    credit = sum((line.functional_credit_amount for line in lines), Decimal(0))
64	    return debit, credit
65	
66	
67	async def list_entries(
68	    session: AsyncSession,
69	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
70	    *,
71	    cursor: str | None,
72	    limit: int,
73	    status: str | None = None,
74	) -> Page[JournalEntry]:
75	    """Keyset-paginated entry list, newest posting first (D-014). Status filter folds into the
76	    cursor fingerprint."""
77	    stmt = select(JournalEntry).where(JournalEntry.tenant_id == tenant_id)
78	    if status is not None:
79	        stmt = stmt.where(JournalEntry.status == EntryStatus(status).value)
80	    return await paginate(
81	        session,
82	        stmt,
83	        order_by=[
84	            OrderKey(JournalEntry.posting_date, SortDirection.DESC),
85	            OrderKey(JournalEntry.created_at, SortDirection.DESC),
86	        ],
87	        pk=JournalEntry.id,
88	        cursor=cursor,
89	        limit=limit,
90	        filters=filter_fingerprint(status),
91	    )

59	) -> Account:

61	    caller omits it; rejects a duplicate code with a ConflictError (the DB UNIQUE is the

180	    no cycle is possible at creation — the cycle guard lives in reparenting below.)"""
181	    existing = (

209	    session: AsyncSession,

211	    group_id: uuid.UUID,
212	    new_parent_id: uuid.UUID | None,
213	) -> AccountGroup:
214	    """Move a group under a new parent, rejecting any move that would create a cycle — a
215	    group can never be its own ancestor (D-021: the tree must stay a tree)."""
216	    group = await _require_group(session, tenant_id, group_id)
217	    if new_parent_id is not None:
218	        if new_parent_id == group_id:
219	            raise ValidationFailedError(
220	                message="A group cannot be its own parent",
221	                code="finance.account_group_cycle",
222	            )
223	        await _require_group(session, tenant_id, new_parent_id)
224	        await _assert_no_cycle(session, tenant_id, group_id, new_parent_id)
225	    group.parent_id = new_parent_id

230	async def _assert_no_cycle(
231	    session: AsyncSession,
232	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
233	    group_id: uuid.UUID,
234	    new_parent_id: uuid.UUID,
235	) -> None:
236	    """Raise if making ``group_id`` a child of ``new_parent_id`` would form a cycle: walk
237	    from new_parent up its parent chain; reaching group_id means group_id is already an
238	    ancestor of the prospective parent. A visited set bounds a pre-existing malformed tree."""
239	    current: uuid.UUID | None = new_parent_id
240	    visited: set[uuid.UUID] = set()
241	    while current is not None:
242	        if current == group_id:
243	            raise ValidationFailedError(
244	                message="Reparenting would create a cycle in the account-group tree",
245	                code="finance.account_group_cycle",
246	            )
247	        if current in visited:
248	            break
249	        visited.add(current)
250	        parent = await _require_group(session, tenant_id, current)
251	        current = parent.parent_id
252

262	        .order_by(AccountGroup.sort_order, AccountGroup.code)
263	    )
264	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())

(with the opaque `partner_id` stamped on the AR line) + **Cr** each revenue line (net) + **Cr** output
tax (to the tax code's payable account). The invoice then claims its gapless system number (`INV-…`),
links invoice→journal (docflow `posts`), sets `open_amount = gross` and status POSTED, and publishes
`CustomerInvoicePosted`. FX translation at posting is the journal engine's standard machinery (D-019).

**Open-item clearing.** A `CustomerReceipt` is created and posted in one step. It validates the
cleared invoices are open, same partner, same currency, none over-allocated; posts a journal entry
(document_type `PAYMENT`): **Cr** AR control (Σ allocated) + **Dr** bank (the cash received), reduces
each invoice's `open_amount` (status → PARTIALLY_PAID/PAID), writes `CustomerReceiptAllocation` rows,
links receipt→invoices (docflow `receipts`), claims its number (`RCT-…`), and publishes
`CustomerReceiptPosted`. `open_amount` is the only stored balance — aging projects over it.

**Realized FX at receipt (D-019).** When the invoice currency ≠ functional, the AR control was
debited at the invoice's posting rate (R1) but the bank receives at the receipt-date rate (R2). The
functional difference per cleared invoice — `functional-at-receipt-rate − functional-at-invoice-rate`
over the cleared transaction amount — is the realized gain/loss, posted to the
`fx_realized_gain`/`fx_realized_loss` posting-default account **inside the same receipt entry** so it
balances in functional. The entry's functional amounts are set explicitly and posted with the journal
engine's `skip_translation`; the realized-FX line is denominated in the functional currency. The
realized-FX math is shared with AP in `service/clearing_fx.py` (AP debits the control to clear, AR
credits it — `control_is_debit` flips the sign; the gain/loss direction inverts accordingly). When
the receipt currency *is* the functional currency, R1 = R2 and there is no FX line.

**Dunning.** `POST /dunning-runs` advances reminder levels. For each OPEN overdue invoice it computes
the level its days-overdue earns from `DUNNING_THRESHOLDS` (level 1 at 7 days past due, 2 at 30, 3 at
60); if that exceeds the invoice's current `dunning_level`, it raises the invoice to it and stamps
`last_dunned_date = as_of`, recording a notice (partner, invoice, new level — a collections proposal
list). It posts **no journal** — dunning is state only. It is idempotent-ish per day: re-running the
same `as_of` advances nothing already at its earned level, so a second same-day run returns an empty
list; a not-yet-overdue invoice stays at level 0.

**Aging.** `GET /ar-aging` is a pure projection over open invoices: each invoice's `open_amount`
lands in the bucket for `as_of − due_date` days (current / 1-30 / 31-60 / 61-90 / over-90), per
partner and rolled up — identical to AP aging on the receivable side.
